mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of FEDFUNDS > 4% months, or the IC > 0.05 over a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 20,000 jobs coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as stronger labor demand is interpreted as a structural improvement in corporate earnings prospects.
failure_condition: Over 3 consecutive months of PAYEMS > +20,000 produce non-positive 60-day returns, or IC < -0.1 over a 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxy HOUST below their 2007 Q4 averages triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals a dual softening in economic output and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 95.0 and HOUST < 550 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >70% of such dual-signal months, or IC > 0.08 over 2 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it suggests accelerating supply capacity and potential for profit expansion.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >40% of 3-month INDPRO expansion phases, or IC < -0.05 over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 5% for the first time in 6 months, it signals labor market slack and a 20-day S&P 500 forward return turns negative as investors anticipate rate cuts and softer equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive in >60% of such rate-cooling episodes, or IC > 0.07 over 18 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls surge above 200,000 jobs accompanied by a decline in unemployment (implied by UNRATE) creates a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust labor market strength and corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are non-positive in >50% of such labor strength episodes, or IC < 0.05 over 2 years.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer confidence ( proxy: HOUST ) above 550 with no offsetting decline in industrial production (INDPRO) predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates sustained consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 550 and INDPRO > 90 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >40% of such demand cycles, or IC < -0.1 over 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL < 210 over 3 months) combined with rising FEDFUNDS produces a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as expectations for future rate stability encourage equity accumulation.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >30% of such low-inflation-FEDFUNDS up-trends, or IC < -0.05 over 6 months.
